name: Beefeater London Dry Gin
production: Botanicals steeped for 24 hours before distillation
Multiple copper pot stills incl. James Burrough's original 268-litre 'Still No. 12'
Nothing added after distillation except water
history: 1820 | Foundations laid at The Chelsea Distillery; James Burrough develops recipe
1876 | Gin production in London begins (Gin Guild)
1953 | Distillery in Kennington since this year (official FAQ; Gin Guild says 1958) [cần kiểm tra]
nose: Fresh citrus, lemon zest, Seville orange
expressions: Beefeater 24 | 45%, adds Japanese sencha, Chinese green tea, grapefruit
Beefeater Burrough's Reserve | limited edition aged 3 weeks in Bordeaux casks that held Lillet
serve_official: G&T 1:3 (50ml gin : 150ml tonic) with lots of ice, garnished with lemon and orange slice
notes: Official site claims it is the only London Dry Gin still made in the city of London. Name refers to the Yeoman Warders of the Tower of London. Nose/palate/finish from Gin Guild (official FAQ gives no tasting notes).
